The jet-lagged numbers in {1, …, 2016} are exactly the numbers 2^j(2^m − 1) with j, m ≥ 1, and there are 51 of them.

**Structure of the sequence.** The first terms are 1, 0, 1, 0, 3, 2, 1, 0, 7, 6, …. The zeros occur at positions 2, 4, 8, 16, …, and the sequence is made of descending runs. For p in (2^k, 2^{k+1}] with k ≥ 0, we have a_p = 2^{k+1} − p, and this formula also gives a_1 = 1.

**Which d are jet-lagged.** Suppose a_{n+r} = a_n + s with r, s ≥ 0 and d = r + s.

- If n and n+r lie in the same run, then a_{n+r} − a_n = −r. This forces s = −r ≥ 0, so r = s = 0 and d = 0, which is not in the set.
- If n lies in run K and n+r lies in run M > K, then a_n = 2^{K+1} − n and a_{n+r} = 2^{M+1} − n − r. So s = 2^{M+1} − 2^{K+1} − r, and therefore d = r + s = 2^{M+1} − 2^{K+1}.
- This value is attainable. Take n = 2^{K+1} and r = 2^{M+1} − 2^{K+1}, so that n + r = 2^{M+1} and s = 0.

Hence the jet-lagged positive integers are exactly d = 2^i − 2^j with i > j ≥ 1. Writing m = i − j, these are d = 2^j(2^m − 1) with j, m ≥ 1. Each such d has a unique pair (j, m), because 2^m − 1 is the odd part of d.

**Counting d ≤ 2016.**

| m | 2^m − 1 | allowed j | count |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1–10 | 10 |
| 2 | 3 | 1–9 | 9 |
| 3 | 7 | 1–8 | 8 |
| 4 | 15 | 1–7 | 7 |
| 5 | 31 | 1–6 | 6 |
| 6 | 63 | 1–5 | 5 |
| 7 | 127 | 1–3 | 3 |
| 8 | 255 | 1–2 | 2 |
| 9 | 511 | 1 | 1 |
| 10 | 1023 | none (2046 > 2016) | 0 |

The total is 10 + 9 + 8 + 7 + 6 + 5 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 51.

ANSWER: 51
